lines.say: a peptide from their own DNA, found naturally in blood (never tested in people)
less weight gain on a high-fat diet, and after ovary removal (mouse studies)
blood glucose and insulin fell in obese or high-fat-fed mice (mouse studies)
better physical capacity in aged mice (mouse study)
fasting glucose or HbA1c checked first, since it lowered blood sugar in mice
possible immune reactions to the peptide or its impurities and clumps, FDA says
theoretical interaction with diabetes medicines; not studied in people

ask: Since MOTS-c has never been tested in people, what would make it worth the risk for me?
